name: FedEx
fiscalYearEnd: May 31 through FY2026; changed to December 31 effective June 1, 2026 (a seven-month transition period, June 1 to December 31, 2026, will be reported on a Transition Report on Form 10-K)
description: FedEx runs the largest all-cargo air fleet and a ground network that delivers packages and freight to more than 220 countries and territories. Customers pay per shipment, with price set by speed (priority, deferred, ground), weight, distance and fuel surcharges, so revenue is shipments times yield per package; the Federal Express segment is 87% of revenue. On June 1, 2026 it spun off FedEx Freight (less-than-truckload trucking) into a separate listed company (FDXF), and from that date reports two segments, Express U.S. Domestic and Express International. It also owns FedEx Office (print and retail shipping counters), FedEx Logistics (customs brokerage and freight forwarding) and FedEx Dataworks (data and analytics), reported together with corporate costs. Operating margin is thin for a network business (7.2% in Federal Express), so network efficiency programs (Network 2.0) matter as much as volume.

businessLines.name: Federal Express (Express U.S. Domestic and Express International)
businessLines.how: Pay-per-shipment delivery fees priced by service speed, weight, zone and surcharges including fuel; about 26% of operating cost is purchased transportation from roughly 5,300 independent service providers.
businessLines.description: Air and ground express package and freight delivery. FY2026 revenue by product: U.S. priority $11,603M, U.S. deferred $5,700M, U.S. ground $37,335M (U.S. domestic package $54,638M); international priority $9,639M, international economy $5,925M, international domestic $4,725M (international export package $15,564M); freight $6,056M; other $1,290M.

businessLines.name: FedEx Freight (spun off June 1, 2026)
businessLines.how: Per-shipment LTL charges (revenue per shipment $386.63 in FY2026) plus fuel surcharge.
businessLines.description: Less-than-truckload freight carrier; no longer consolidated after June 1, 2026.

businessLines.name: Corporate, other and eliminations (FedEx Office, FedEx Logistics, FedEx Dataworks, corporate)
businessLines.how: Retail print and shipping fees (Office), customs brokerage and forwarding fees (Logistics), data services (Dataworks); corporate costs are unallocated.
businessLines.description: Segments below reporting thresholds plus corporate costs.
